summary: Rigolet Airport (YRG) is a small regional airport serving the Inuit community of Rigolet in Labrador, Canada. Situated on the northern shore of Lake Melville along the Hamilton Inlet, it provides a vital air link for this remote settlement of approximately 300 residents. The airport primarily supports medevac services, government travel, and passenger flights connecting Rigolet to larger Labrador hubs like Happy Valley-Goose Bay.
faqs:
Q: What airlines serve Rigolet Airport?
A: Rigolet Airport is primarily served by regional carriers operating flights to and from Happy Valley-Goose Bay, with service typically operated by small aircraft suited to the remote location.

Q: How large is Rigolet Airport?
A: It is a small unpaved airport with a single runway, designed to accommodate small turboprop aircraft rather than larger commercial jets.

Q: When is the best time to fly to Rigolet?
A: Summer months (June through September) offer the most reliable weather and additional travel options, including seasonal ferry service as an alternative.

Q: Is the airport open year-round?
A: Yes, but winter weather can cause delays or cancellations due to snow and icing conditions common in Labrador.
transport_tips: The airport is located within walking distance of the Rigolet town center, so ground transportation is rarely needed. Visitors should confirm flights in advance, as schedules are limited and weather-related cancellations are common. Many travelers combine their trip with the seasonal ferry service from Happy Valley-Goose Bay during summer months for a more scenic arrival.
local_tip: Pack for variable weather year-round and bring any specialty supplies you need, as the community store has limited stock and flights are subject to cancellation—flexibility and patience are essential when traveling to Rigolet.
